title: rank1 kv256 Llama-2 PPL=752 root cause: SVD calibration stochasticity
summary: PPL=752 is NOT reproducible. 3 runs same config: 752.71 / 161.09 / 788.11 (4.9x spread). Filters look healthy (norm=1, no NaN) but 5% of heads drift near-orthogonal across runs (|cos|<0.5 on 48-57/1024 heads per pair). Rank=1 uniquely fragile under torch.svd_lowrank(niter=2) — 1D subspace is sign/direction ambiguous; rank=2 kv=256 PPL=353 is stable by comparison. calib=128 gave PPL=372, so more data does NOT fix it — the issue is niter=2 convergence, not sample size.
root_cause: src/memory/qfilters/calibration.py:219 torch.svd_lowrank(mat, q=rank, niter=2) — randomized SVD with only 2 subspace iterations; RNG state varies run-to-run because it depends on model-load/fork order
recommended_fix: Option A (preferred): in calibration.py use torch.linalg.svd exact when rank<=2 (cost negligible at D=128); fall back to svd_lowrank niter=7 for rank>=3. Option B (cheaper): torch.manual_seed(0) before calibration + niter=7. Cost of Option A: ~milliseconds per model (32 layers × 32 heads × exact 128-dim SVD). DO NOT APPLY without owner review.

verdict: Tier-2 fix3 (zero-init slot_to_hidden) FALSIFIED: step-1 PPL=62.64 vs predicted [16,18]; final PPL 2311/25346 vs contract ≤25. Root cause is phantom-logit softmax pollution: k=64 slot keys with value 0 contribute exp(0)=1 terms to the softmax denominator, attenuating H-attention by S_H/(k+S_H) per layer; compounded over 32 layers this is 60-90% signal loss on the fix2-unmasked second half of each chunk. RMSNorm-of-zero hypothesis refuted empirically (RMSNorm(0)=0 exactly). 1107M trainable (vs predicted 540M) is because hidden_to_slot is ALSO a Linear and harvested, but receives zero gradient (writeback is inert per Tier-2 §2).
fix: Flamingo-style OUTPUT-side gate. Replace concat-joint forward with two forwards: bypass_h = wrapped_layer(H) and ext_h = wrapped_layer([slots,H]). Combine as next_hidden = bypass_h + tanh(alpha) * (ext_h[k:] - bypass_h) with alpha=nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(())) init 0. Also freeze hidden_to_slot (inert) and drop fix2 T/2 cutoff (no longer needed). Revert slot_to_hidden to std=0.02 init.
fallback: If step-0 != 16.50 exactly: bypass path is contaminated — add unit test against vanilla Llama. If training explodes: drop lr to 1e-4, clip to 0.1. If gate stuck at 0: init alpha=1e-3. If all fail: escalate to Stage-1.5 redesign (shrink to N=64 k=8, or cross-attn side-channel at LM head).

question: Why does key clustering (pairwise_cos rising to +0.004) fail to improve top1_sim above floor? Is InfoNCE the right fix?
conclusion: DOUBLE FAILURE MODE identified. (1) Clustering is statistically significant (16.4sigma) but physically tiny: centroid_norm=7.7%, 99.4% of variance is in residual. Common-mode shift from clustering is softmax-invariant => zero effect on routing selectivity. (2) STE gradient from LM loss is blocked by uniform slot values: all slots init from same hidden pool, so slot_to_hidden(slots[i]) ≈ slot_to_hidden(slots[j]) => d(LM)/d(scores_i) is near-uniform for all i => no differentiation signal to Q_sel or slot_keys through LM path. Expected top1_sim from pairwise_cos=+0.004 is theoretically 0.042 (same as ETF), but STE bottleneck prevents both routes from learning.

Clustering is real but insufficient because (a) common-mode softmax cancels routing gain, (b) LM gradient path to slot_keys is blocked by uniform slot values. InfoNCE bypasses BOTH failure modes: operates directly on slot_keys via nk[pos_idx] without going through slot_to_hidden(slots), gradient magnitude ~T*(1-1/N)≈10 non-vanishing at all states.

question: Why does VQ-EMA routing collapse after initial peak (top1_sim 0.211→0.003)? Why does Arm C (InfoNCE+norm_cap) resist? Propose Fix Y.
conclusion: Root cause is the classic VQ codebook collapse / dead slot problem (van den Oord 2017, §A.1). vq_ema_update() only updates slots in 'assigned = new_count > 0'; dead slots (~97% per step under top-1-only with N=512) never get revived. Popular slots' keys converge toward shared query centroid via EMA → pairwise_cos rises 0.0→0.625 → routing degenerates to uniform → top1_sim collapses. Fix Y = dead slot revival: detect ema_cluster_count < 0.5, reinit slot_keys from random batch query, reset EMA state.
key_finding: Dead slot revival is absent from vq_ema_update(). This is the primary causal mechanism for collapse. All production VQ systems (VQ-VAE, VQ-VAE-2, HuBERT, EnCodec) include it. retrieved_norm growth is a symptom/amplifier, not primary cause. Arm C resists because InfoNCE provides active key repulsion (contrastive loss pushes k_neg away from query) that counteracts VQ-EMA's convergence tendency; pairwise_cos=0.10 Arm C vs 0.625 Arms A/B.

question: Why did Fix Y fail, and what is Fix Z? Why does VQ-EMA key convergence happen even with InfoNCE qa=0.05?
conclusion: Fix Y failed due to TWO independent bugs + ONE architectural conflict. Bug #1: ema_cluster_count only decays on assigned slots (selector.py L253-258), so unassigned slots stay at init value 1.0 forever and revival threshold 0.5 is unreachable — explains dead_revived=0 for entire Y2 run. Bug #2: vq_ema_update() writes slot_keys.data[assigned]=new_keys inside forward(), OVERWRITING Adam updates from InfoNCE every step (Adam displacement ≈2e-4 vs EMA overwrite ≈1.0 magnitude). Raising qa does NOT help — opposition is structural not scalar. Architectural conflict: mean-pooled Q_sel queries collapse to LM common mode, so EMA-of-queries centroids all converge regardless of bug fixes. Fix Z = remove VQ-EMA entirely + FREEZE slot_keys to random unit-norm Gaussians + rely on load_balance_loss to train Q_sel.
